topic: Important Dams and River Projects (Static GK)
description: A comprehensive study guide covering major dams and multi-purpose river valley projects in India, which are crucial for water management, irrigation, and hydroelectric power generation.

sections.title: Multi-purpose River Valley Projects
sections.description: Projects designed to achieve multiple objectives simultaneously, such as flood control, power generation, and irrigation.

key_concepts.explanation: River valley projects that serve various purposes at once, including irrigation, flood control, hydroelectric power generation, navigation, and pisciculture (fish farming).

historical_events.significance: It is the first multi-purpose river valley project of independent India, modeled after the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) of the USA.

important_facts.fact: India's first Prime Minister, Pt. Jawaharlal Nehru, proudly referred to the multi-purpose river valley projects as the 'Temples of Modern India'.

sections.title: Major Dams of North and East India
sections.description: Crucial water projects built across the Himalayan and Eastern peninsular rivers.

geographical_data.key_characteristics: It is the highest dam in India, with a towering height of 260.5 meters.

geographical_data.location_or_origin: Sutlej River, Himachal Pradesh and Punjab
geographical_data.key_characteristics: It is the largest gravity dam in India. Its vast reservoir is known as the Gobind Sagar Lake.
It is the longest earthen dam in the world, with a total length of 25.8 km including the dykes.
Its reservoir is called Govind Ballabh Pant Sagar, which holds the record for being the largest artificial lake in India.

sections.title: Major Projects of Central and Western India
sections.description: Key dams located on prominent rivers like the Narmada, Tapti, and Chambal.

geographical_data.key_characteristics: The largest dam of the Narmada Valley Project, providing water and electricity to four states (Gujarat, MP, Maharashtra, Rajasthan).
It possesses the largest water storage capacity among all reservoirs in India.
The second largest reservoir in Gujarat after Sardar Sarovar, also known as Vallabh Sagar.
It is one of the four major dams built under the Chambal Valley Project.

sections.title: Major Dams of South India
sections.description: Massive irrigation and hydroelectric structures built on the Krishna, Kaveri, and Periyar rivers.

geographical_data.location_or_origin: Krishna River, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh
geographical_data.key_characteristics: It is officially recognized as the largest masonry dam in the world.
Situated on a major tributary of the Krishna river, its reservoir is famously called Pampa Sagar.
One of the oldest and largest dams in India; its massive reservoir is known as the Stanley Reservoir.
It is a double curvature arch dam constructed between the Kuravan and Kurathi hills, making it one of the highest arch dams in Asia.

sections.title: Other Important Projects and Records
sections.description: Frequently asked one-liners and unique features of various Indian dams.

key_associations.extra_info: It is highly notable for featuring the first underground power station in the whole of South East Asia.
Due to its massive electricity generation capacity, it is often called the 'Lifeline of Maharashtra'.
It is officially known and recorded as the Lal Bahadur Shastri Dam.

important_facts.fact: The Kallanai Dam (also known as Grand Anicut), located on the Kaveri River in Tamil Nadu, is the oldest working dam in India, built by King Karikalan of the Chola Dynasty in the 2nd century AD.
The Uri Dam and Baglihar Dam are highly strategic projects located on the Jhelum and Chenab rivers respectively, in the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir.
